Summary Description: Dr. Javier A. Jo is a leading researcher at the University of Oklahoma whose work sits at the intersection of biomedical optics, machine learning, and translational imaging. His research program spans the development and application of multispectral autofluorescence lifetime imaging (maFLIM) for in vivo tissue characterization, with a strong emphasis on unsupervised and contrastive learning to uncover clinically meaningful structure in high-dimensional imaging data without relying on lesion labels. He has contributed to the design and analysis of handheld, dual‑excitation FLIM systems and hardware-software co-design for real-time metabolic imaging, including REDOX mapping and lifetime mapping across multiple spectral channels. Jo has also explored fairness in ML models applied to medical imaging, demonstrating that tissue-location biases can persist in maFLIM-based diagnostics and proposing tissue-location–aware fine-tuning to improve cross-site robustness. In addition to oral cancer applications, his work extends to breast imaging through pseudo-color augmentation and multi-view CADx pipelines, illustrating a broad interest in leveraging segmentation, contour information, and multi-modal data to enhance diagnostic performance. Across these efforts, Jo emphasizes clinically actionable metrics, rigorous validation (including cross-validation, compare with gold standards like pathology, and statistical significance testing), and the translation of imaging data into tools that support decision-making in biopsy workflows and patient management.
